title: Meta Stock Rises 3.4% on Reports of Amazon Muse Talks (Nov 25)
summary: Meta Platforms (META) closed at $609.89 on Nov 25, +3.40%, as Fortune reported Meta and Amazon held talks on ending Amazon's block of the Muse agent.
body_markdown:
## Why Meta Stock Rose


According to[Fortune](https://fortune.com/2026/11/25/exclusive-amazon-meta-talks-deal-muse-ai-shopping-agent-blockade/) , which published its exclusive before the open on November 25, Meta and Amazon have held talks on multiple occasions about connecting Muse to Amazon's store and ending a blockade Amazon imposed two months ago. Fortune reported that search results and advertising are the two major issues under negotiation, and that any deal is expected to require sign-off from the CEOs of both companies.


Amazon blocked Muse in September, saying its access would break Amazon's user agreements, per Fortune. Meta and Amazon declined to comment, and Meta issued no statement or filing on the talks.


As reported by[BigGo Finance](https://finance.biggo.com/news/77d3b159-67e6-4aa2-b0fa-f527177e250f) , Meta shares bucked the trend to close higher as reports of the Muse talks emerged, recovering from an early decline in the session.


## META Stock Analysis: Supporting Factors and Risks


### Supporting Factors


- Fortune reported that more than 10 million people in the US and Canada had set up Muse as of October, and described the agent as Meta's biggest consumer AI hit to date.
- Muse already works with other retailers. Fortune listed Shopify, Walmart and Best Buy among its earlier retail partners and said Meta plans to take a small fee from transactions, while BigGo Finance reported that[Walmart (WMT)](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/wmt/) announced on November 24 that shoppers could buy its Black Friday deals through Muse.


### Risks


- No agreement is in place. Fortune said discussions are fluid and it is unclear if or how soon a deal will be struck, noting that Muse could in theory bypass the advertisements on Amazon's website.
- According to[Reuters, via MyJoyOnline](https://www.myjoyonline.com/meta-pauses-class-c-share-issuance-amid-shareholder-lawsuit/) , Meta said on November 23 that it will not issue its planned Class C shares while it faces shareholder litigation in Delaware, with a trial scheduled for April 19, 2027. That delays a planned $60 billion at-the-market stock sale meant to help fund its AI investments.
